BiblicalUsage: This word for bondage or servitude occurs three times, all in the prayers of the returned exiles. Ezra confesses, 'we were bondmen; yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage'; and Nehemiah's prayer recalls how the fathers 'appointed a captain to return to their bondage' in Egypt.
TheologicalSignificance: Twice the exiles name their bondage in the same breath as God's mercy — 'yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage.' I believe that is the deepest comfort in the word: bondage is real, and so is God's presence inside it, and He does not wait for us to be free before He shows mercy.
